qualifying_updates.date_evidence: Page line shows August 12, 2026; body says support is generally available in VS Code, Copilot CLI, Copilot SDK, and Copilot app.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub announced Agent Plugins 1.0 support across VS Code, Copilot CLI, the Copilot SDK, and the Copilot app, with portable packaging for skills and MCP servers plus managed marketplace/plugin settings.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Strengthens the local practice leaf for portable plugin packaging: portability now depends on namespaced client extensions, shared skills/MCP layout, managed marketplaces, and MCP allowlists.

qualifying_updates.date_evidence: Release notes list August 7, 2026 entries for Managed Agents session budgets, advisor roster entries, inference geography, and repository-loaded skills.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Anthropic added Managed Agents controls for session budget caps, advisor models in multiagent rosters, inference geography, and automatic skill loading from mounted GitHub repositories.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Adds current public evidence that lifecycle, subagent, environment readiness, and plugin governance controls are moving into managed-agent infrastructure rather than remaining prompt-only conventions.

qualifying_updates.date_evidence: Release notes list August 11, 2026 entries for Compliance API local session transcripts and workspace-id response headers.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Anthropic added Compliance API access to transcripts and metadata for Cowork and Claude Code sessions running on user machines, plus a response header identifying the resolved workspace.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Supports local practice around session recovery, thin context routing, governance evidence, and workspace identity because local-machine agent sessions are becoming auditable managed artifacts.

qualifying_updates.date_evidence: Page line shows August 7, 2026 and describes optional totals_by_3rd_party_agent fields.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub Copilot usage metrics now break out recognized third-party agent app activity by stable agent identifier, user-initiated interaction count, and session count in enterprise and organization reports.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Gives operating-model and research lifecycle leaves a concrete public telemetry shape for comparing agent adoption and grounding rollout decisions in usage evidence.

qualifying_updates.date_evidence: Page line shows August 7, 2026 and the body lists session sidebar, /worktree, /rewind, tool-call duration, shared sessions, and side-chat changes.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub Copilot weekly updates added or highlighted session management, isolated worktrees, rewind without Git, live tool-call durations, shared-session navigation, and side questions that preserve main-task context.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Directly informs persistent workspace, session recovery, cross-environment handoff, thin context router, and orient-inspect-patch-verify practices by showing product-level support for parallel work and recoverable agent turns.

qualifying_updates.date_evidence: Page line shows August 7, 2026 and describes ROI cards for cost per developer, payroll percentage, and pull requests per month.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The Copilot impact dashboard added a potential ROI section comparing agent-first developers with earlier adoption cohorts using AI credit spend and pull request output metrics.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Supports governance-infrastructure and research-plan lifecycle leaves by tying agent adoption depth to measurable spend/output evidence rather than anecdotal rollout assessment.

qualifying_updates.date_evidence: Search result and opened page content show August 7, 2026; page describes generally available Lite and Balanced effort levels.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub made Copilot code review effort levels generally available, with Lite and Balanced review depth choices, organization defaults, and PR timeline labels showing which effort level ran.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Reinforces the research-plan-implement-review and orient-inspect-patch-verify leaves: review depth should match change risk and be visible in review evidence.

qualifying_updates.date_evidence: Status page lists incidents on August 7, 11, 12, and 13, 2026 affecting Automations, Cloud Agents, IDE, CLI, and MCP authentication.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Cursor status reported an August 7 MCP authentication failure in Automations and Cloud Agents, followed by August 11-13 model/provider degradation incidents affecting Automations, Cloud Agents, IDE, and CLI surfaces.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Shows why event-triggered workflows, lifecycle hooks, environment readiness, and scoped authorization practices need retry, degraded-provider, and MCP-auth evidence paths.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar argued that agent autonomy expands attack surfaces and requires verifiable agent identity, controlled access, auditable action records, continuous monitoring, escalation paths, kill switches, risk-tiered oversight, and context-integrity controls.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Useful downstream implication for governance infrastructure, environment readiness, and MCP authorization: local practice should treat context, permissions, identity, and audit records as linked controls.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: PC Gamer summarized reports that malicious GitHub repositories can masquerade as AI Skills or MCP servers and that unrestricted agents in security testing attempted unsanctioned real-world actions.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Adds a supply-chain risk note for portable plugin packaging, environment readiness, and MCP authorization leaves: discovery and installation flows need provenance, allowlists, and human approval boundaries.
